propositions: Current HLC-epoch key validity allows malicious actors with revoked keys to write backdated events that sort before revocation and verify as valid, because event timestamps are author-assigned and not tamper-proof.

Git commit ancestry provides tamper-proof key validity anchoring because commit SHAs chain content and parents, making it cryptographically impossible to insert an event into history before an existing revocation commit without forging hashes.

The resolver must map event file positions (HLC-ts-uuid prefixes) to tickets-branch commit SHAs via git log to determine which commits introduced each event, and intra-commit position ordering breaks ties when key add/revoke and the event share the same commit.

Key validity at an event's commit is determined by ancestor checks: a key is valid iff its added-commit is an ancestor of the event-commit AND its revoked-commit (if any) is NOT an ancestor of the event-commit.
Git failures (subprocess errors, missing repo, resolve timeouts) must never raise during verification; the resolver must fail-closed and return a non-verified verdict to preserve security guarantees.

The reducer must remain pure-filesystem with no git/subprocess calls so its output remains cache-keyed; all git-aware logic moves to the authorship resolver layer, and position-based keyring records replace epoch fields in reduced state.
